# Native OAuth grants, source handoff for 2026-10-04

The default PostgreSQL agent journal previously refused every OAuth grant operation with `oauth_unavailable`. This packet implements the existing `grants`, `getGrant` and `setGrant` contracts on a dedicated native table. Browser consent and revocation remain the existing authenticated human routes; this persistence change does not authorize a caller or permit deployment.

`agent.agent_oauth_grants` holds the exact non-secret subject/client/workspace binding, immutable globally unique integration identity, issuer, expiry, revocation state and bounded project/environment/app/scope arrays. It stores no OAuth token, refresh token, provider key, arbitrary Grant document, browser duration or derived authorization digest. Input is detached and validated before the first await. Reads name the exact subject and workspace, and single-grant reads also name the client. Expired and revoked records remain available for withdrawal and renewal. A scoped list over 100 rows refuses instead of truncating authority.

`setGrant` uses one READ COMMITTED transaction and a transaction-scoped advisory lock derived from the exact subject/workspace pair. This serializes creation even when there is no existing row. New bindings enforce the browser's existing 50 retained-grant quota; same-identity renewal, attenuation and revocation remain possible at the limit. Revoked and expired rows count toward that existing quota and are not pruned. Hash collisions cause only extra serialization. The binding unique constraint, global integration primary key and immutable identity trigger independently prevent replacement or cross-tenant adoption. A conflicting identity or failed native write returns a fixed refusal. Direct operator/service-role SQL remains privileged storage access, not a human consent endpoint; the journal quota governs journal writers.

The new migration is `supabase/migrations/0015_agent_oauth_grants.sql`, agent ledger version 3, `agent-oauth-grants-v1`. The shared frozen `AGENT_CONTROL_MIGRATIONS` registry is the canonical name/version/file inventory. Ordinary non-OAuth journal work still requires versions 1 and 2 only. OAuth methods require all three known version/name pairs and refuse absent or conflicting schema. The historical agent ledger has no checksum column: this packet does not claim ledger checksum verification or rewrite accepted migrations. The existing platform checksum verifier is unchanged.

Migration 15 applies transactionally, refuses incompatible partial tables or client policies, and checks actual column order/types/nullability, constraint type/key/definition/validation flags and enforcing primary/unique index structure before recording success. The new read-only `scripts/agent/verify-schema.ts` shares the registry and shape descriptors, uses native catalogs under a scoped `pg_catalog` search path, and verifies RLS/no client policies and least-privilege role boundaries. Constraint names alone cannot certify `CHECK (true)` or a UNIQUE key on the wrong columns. The deparsed canonical shape targets the current pinned PostgreSQL 16 lane; a different native representation refuses and needs independent compatibility review. The schema checks use PostgreSQL's documented [constraint catalog](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/catalog-pg-constraint.html), [index catalog](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/catalog-pg-index.html) and [native definition functions](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/functions-info.html).

The table enables RLS with no client policies. `service_role` receives SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE only, with no DELETE/TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER; `anon`, `authenticated` and PUBLIC receive no table privileges. The validation and identity functions do not grant write authority. Canonical CI role stand-ins must retain their existing non-superuser topology, with BYPASSRLS only for `service_role`. Native SET ROLE controls prove SQL privilege/RLS behavior; they do not prove a live Supabase project's role membership or exposed API configuration.

Run the complete canonical migration script in numeric order. Historical migrations 6 and 7 grant all agent tables to the service role, so reapplying an older migration alone after 15 can restore DELETE; the verifier rejects that state. Reapplying the complete script applies 15 last and restores the least-privilege boundary. The script calls the shared agent verifier rather than introducing another ledger count/string. Its existing platform verification remains intact. The agent verifier accepts only explicit approved `SUPABASE_DB_URL` configuration, does not load local environment files or accept a URL through argv, emits fixed diagnostics, and closes its client.

The new suite is `OAuth resource grant journal [postgres]` in `tests/agent-control/pg-oauth-grants.test.ts`. Its 47 expanded literal identities are frozen in the accompanying CASE-CONTRACT receipt. Required execution sets `ZENITH_TEST_PG_OAUTH_GRANTS_REQUIRED=1`, `ZENITH_CONTRACT_POSTGRES=1` and an explicitly owned disposable `SUPABASE_DB_URL`; missing prerequisites fail before pools/hooks. Root must apply the canonical migrations first and provide administrative CREATEDB authority for positively owned isolated compatibility/fault databases. The suite never creates server roles or changes the configured shared schema for fault fixtures. It uses two genuine independent PostgreSQL clients and checks backend identity. Its default-journal read uses the existing real process singleton. The upstream VerifiedOAuth input in binding checks is explicitly a protocol model.

## Revision 2, canonical trigger and function enforcement

Revision 1 remains immutable and correction-required. Its read-only verifier recognized the identity trigger's name/enabled state/function OID without proving UPDATE timing and row coverage. A same-named DELETE-only trigger could pass that check while service_role changed a grant identity through UPDATE. It also recognized CHECK helper calls without checking the helper's implementation.

This separate four-path correction changes the shared registry, read-only verifier, native grant fixture and this handoff. Migration 0015 and every earlier migration are byte-exact. Journal persistence methods, quota and non-OAuth compatibility are unchanged. The verifier requires exactly one noninternal trigger with the original function and the canonical BEFORE UPDATE FOR EACH ROW type, no column/WHEN/argument/constraint/deferred/transition-table variant. It compares both migration functions' exact source, language, signature/return type, invoker mode, search path, strictness, volatility, parallel and other execution flags. PUBLIC/client execution of either function refuses; service_role retains canonical execution.

The 47 original native identities and callbacks remain unchanged. There are 22 additional native controls: eight trigger faults and fourteen identity/helper function faults. The DELETE-only fixture demonstrates actual scoped service_role identity replacement before verifier refusal; the weakened helper accepts an empty required ID array before refusal. Canonical unchanged migration reapplication restores verification in each disposable fixture. Repair proves current schema, and does not undo historical data written under a corrupted schema. The extra-trigger fixture removes only its explicitly owned extra trigger before reapplication.

All controls use the existing mandatory `ZENITH_TEST_PG_OAUTH_GRANTS_REQUIRED=1` flag and physical PostgreSQL lane. Upstream OAuth identity remains modeled. Schema verification and grant persistence do not prove native OAuth dispatch provenance, consent, provider token validation or browser execution. The author ran no imports, tests, compiler, lint, services or database operations. Independent source review, actual native PostgreSQL 69-case execution and canonical gate registration remain root work; no runtime acceptance is inferred here.

PostgreSQL's [trigger catalog](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/catalog-pg-trigger.html), [function catalog](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/16/catalog-pg-proc.html) and [PostgreSQL 16 trigger bits](https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_16_STABLE/src/include/catalog/pg_trigger.h) define the inspected fields. Native default/deparsing compatibility still requires the actual root lane.

## Revision 3, native cold catalog compatibility

Root's owned PostgreSQL 16.15 cold migration failed inside unpublished migration 0015 with the fixed constraint incompatibility error. The preserved prefix-only transaction readback identified two source mismatches. Native primary and unique constraints have `connoinherit=true`, while native CHECK constraints have `connoinherit=false`. The migration and verifier incorrectly required false for every constraint. The issuer CHECK's actual native deparser also retains a separate group around the expanded BETWEEN bounds. Its stored semantics enforce the same 1 to 2048 length and HTTPS prefix as before. The root failure and prefix readback remain immutable; no successful grant or dispatch execution is inferred from them.

This separate five-path incremental correction starts from the exact frozen revision 2 candidate tree `472f4dee3bea258d0e2feb3ff18a42e65fe99560`. It changes only unpublished migration 0015's canonical flag/issuer comparisons, the shared issuer definition, the verifier's corresponding type-specific flag check, two additive native cases and this handoff. Both admission paths require the native inheritance flag to equal its constraint-type expectation; neither ignores it. All column, CHECK, identity, unique-index, trigger, function, RLS, role and least-privilege checks remain mandatory. No accepted 0006, 0007 or platform migration history is edited, and the table/constraint definitions and grants in 0015 are unchanged.

The original 69 native case identities and callbacks remain exact. Two new cases bring the frozen contract to 71: cold native catalog equality with the actual issuer definition and type-specific inheritance flags, followed by safe reapplication; and same-named CHECK NO INHERIT refusal by both verifier and migration without recording a version-3 ledger row. These use the existing positively owned disposable scratch databases, native PostgreSQL catalog and canonical migration bytes. They add no server roles, shared-schema faults, trigger disable, catalog mutation, provider token, privilege fallback or skip allowance. The suite keeps `ZENITH_TEST_PG_OAUTH_GRANTS_REQUIRED=1` and its unchanged physical PostgreSQL prerequisites. Canonical gate registration of the two new names is a separate owned lane.
